paper.title: Algorithm 828: DNSPLIN1: Discrete nonlinear spline interpolation
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 29(4), 458-468 (TOMS 828, Dec 2003)

code.note: Fortran 77 shar archive. Remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run it with sh to create Fortran77/Dp/ (Makefile, driver.f, src.f, dblas.f, lapack.f, data1..5, res1..5). The Makefile target Res1 runs ./driver < data1 (its stdout to Res1_1 and dnsplin1.prt to Res1_2). Check the output against the shipped res1.

claim.location: The shipped reference output res1 in the 828.gz archive, data set 1 (Fortran77/Dp/res1). Row 2 (the second value after the count 241) is 0.565126291685656D-01.
claim.metric: The second interpolated value printed by driver on data1 (Res1), compared with 0.565126291685656D-01 from res1.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled and was not read.

values.name: driver on data1, row 2 of res1

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. Values are printed to 15 significant digits (about 1e-17 absolute at 0.0565), so the print rounding is far below 1e-12. 1e-12 absolute leaves room for libm and compiler differences in a double-precision spline. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: a Fortran compile and one run on 7 points.
cost.data_size: None beyond the archive (data1 is 7 points).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: DNSPLIN1 is a discrete spline interpolation code with a shipped reference output for a 7-point data set, so the claim is a checkable number that the code must compute.
